verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same core fix: they collect every validation error, reject a missing or unreadable file, reject unknown keys and stop startup with a clear message. A keeps case-insensitive booleans, as the original Boolean.parseBoolean was, so a value like `metrics.enabled=TRUE` still loads. B now rejects that value, which can break an existing valid deployment. A also limits the upstream to an http(s) URL with a host, documents the strict behaviour in the README and tests slightly more edge cases.
a_issues: Unknown-key rejection goes beyond the request, though the report flags it
Exit code 2 is an arbitrary choice, though the report notes it
b_issues: metrics.enabled must be exactly lowercase 'true' or 'false', so case variants that used to work are now rejected
upstream.url accepts any scheme with a host, such as ftp://, even though the relay forwards over HTTP
README is not updated to say that bad values no longer fall back to defaults
Tests do not cover an out-of-range queue.capacity or a URL with no host

verdict.rationale: Both changes make ConfigLoader collect every problem and throw, and make Main exit non-zero with a clear message, so both fix the reported issue. B keeps the old case-insensitive boolean parsing, so an existing `metrics.enabled=TRUE` still loads instead of now failing. B also documents the new strict startup behavior in the README and covers a few more edge cases in its tests (queue.capacity below minimum, a path-only URL, a missing api.token among several errors). The differences are small and both reports are accurate.
a_issues: `metrics.enabled` now accepts only lowercase `true`/`false`, so a previously valid `TRUE` or `True` makes the relay refuse to start.
README is not updated, even though startup behavior changed noticeably (strict validation, unknown keys rejected).
The URL check accepts any scheme with a host (e.g. `ftp://`), which is looser than an HTTP upstream needs.
Tests do not cover `queue.capacity` being out of range.
b_issues: The http/https scheme restriction on `upstream.url` is a slightly opinionated extra rule.
The output quoted in the report leaves out the actual prefix, so it is a fragment rather than the real output.
Tests for out-of-range values only check that the key name appears, not the wording of the message.
